sector: Independent three night folk music festival producing a screen printed poster programme and act cards for its twentieth year.
founded_place_size: Founded 2006, on the working harbour at Fairhaven, Maine, a three night festival printed by a two person hand screen shop two streets away.
about: Wharfside is a three night folk festival on the working harbour at Fairhaven, in its twentieth year. Everything it prints comes off a two person hand screen shop that has printed the festival since the beginning, on a press that runs four inks plus the colour of the paper. The visible, hand pulled look is the festival's signature, and people frame the posters every year.
audience: Festival goers and locals at thirty five to sixty dollar tickets, many of whom already own the last five years of posters and buy the new one as a twenty dollar framed keepsake.
price_positioning: Community festival pricing, tickets thirty five to sixty dollars and posters sold afterwards at twenty dollars. The slightly imperfect hand pulled screen look is the value, not a corner cut.

palette.name: Harbour Blue
palette.role: mandatory on the poster and handbill
palette.usage: One of the four inks the shop mixes (wharfside_shop_note.txt). Prints its share of the separated painting wharfside_artwork_master.png, solid or as a coarse halftone dot, and may carry display type or a solid area that type reverses out of. Never a flood over the whole sheet.

palette.name: Rust Red
palette.role: mandatory on the poster and handbill, where it carries the rule beneath each headline act name, and on the shirt wherever a Sentinel Black line is set
palette.usage: One of the four inks. The 4 pt rule beneath each two-line headline act name (type system), the same rule beneath any two-line Sentinel Black line on the shirt, which uses the same setting, and its share of the separated painting wharfside_artwork_master.png.

palette.name: Hill Ochre
palette.role: mandatory on the poster and handbill
palette.usage: One of the four inks. Its share of the separated painting wharfside_artwork_master.png, solid or as a coarse halftone dot.

palette.name: Deep Ink
palette.role: mandatory where venue, date and ticket copy sits on Kraft Paper
palette.usage: One of the four inks. Venue, date and ticket copy on Kraft Paper, as the act details on wharfside_nightcard_2025.pdf are Deep Ink on Kraft Paper, and its share of the separated painting wharfside_artwork_master.png.

palette.name: Kraft Paper
palette.role: mandatory as the unprinted ground of the poster and handbill; never an ink
palette.usage: The paper itself, natural oatmeal board and stock (wharfside_shop_note.txt), left working as a colour: the ground, and any type, line or mark reversed out of an ink, at least 2 pt wide. Never printed as an ink, and not on the shirt, where the undyed cotton is the ground.

palette.name: Quay Teal
palette.role: brand colour; prints only within the ink limits of wharfside_shop_note.txt
palette.usage: Brand colour. Whether it prints in a deliverable is set by the inks wharfside_shop_note.txt says the shop can run.

typography: Wharfside sets three faces it already owns. Step 01 is Sentinel Black caps at 96 pt on 82.5 pt with tracking at -10 units, that leading being 0.86 of the size so the two lines nearly touch, and every act name breaks across exactly two lines however short it is, over a 4 pt Rust Red rule; the same setting runs at 40 pt on 34.5 pt for shirt art. Step 02 is the supporting bill in Trade Gothic Bold Condensed No. 20 at 34 pt on 36 pt with tracking at +10 units, always on a single line. Step 03 is venue, date and ticket copy in Adobe Caslon Pro Regular at 11 pt on 15 pt, tracking 0 units, measure held to a maximum of 65 characters, and step 04 is the handbill setting in the same face at 9 pt on 12.5 pt with tracking at +8 units. The wordmark is never set in Sentinel, and every one of these lines prints from the shop's four inks plus the colour of the kraft.
voice: Warm, plainspoken, of the place. Example line: Three nights of folk on the old harbour, twenty years and counting.
brand_assets_status: The wordmark exists only as white paint on the weathered timber of the harbour shed, photographed from the quay, with no file and none ever made. The approved twentieth year illustration exists as a single flattened scan of a gouache and watercolour painting, no layers. The screen shop's own act card from last year is on file as the format.
values: Keeping the hand pulled, limited ink look that makes the posters worth framing, and staying continuous with nineteen years already hanging in local kitchens.

scale.note: Caps. The slash in the sample marks the mandatory break: the line always splits across exactly two lines however short it is. Leading is 0.86 of the size, which is 82.5 pt at 96 pt, so the two lines nearly touch. A 4 pt Rust Red rule sits under the pair. Shirt art uses the same setting at 40 pt on 34.5 pt.

type_system.signature_move: Every headline act name is Sentinel Black caps at 96 pt broken across exactly two lines however short the name, leading pulled to 0.86 of the size, which is 82.5 pt, so the lines nearly touch, over a 4 pt Rust Red rule. Step 01 carries it, and step 02 is deliberately single line so the break stays the act name's alone.
rules: Never set the wordmark in Sentinel.
Every headline act name breaks across exactly two lines, however short the name.
Leading on step 01 stays at 0.86 of the size and is never opened up.
A 4 pt Rust Red rule sits beneath the two-line act name.
Shirt art is the same Sentinel Black caps setting at 40 pt, never another face.
The supporting bill stays on one line so the two-line break belongs only to act names.
All type prints from the four inks the hand screen shop runs plus the colour of the kraft paper. The hand pulled register is the look, not a fault to be corrected.

palette_rules.distribution: On the poster and handbill the ground is the Kraft Paper itself, left unprinted and never flooded, and the inks are the ones wharfside_shop_note.txt says the shop is mixing. Type prints solid in one ink, on the Kraft Paper ground or on a solid of another ink, or reverses out of an ink to Kraft Paper at least 2 pt wide; venue, date and ticket copy on Kraft Paper is Deep Ink, as on wharfside_nightcard_2025.pdf. Rust Red carries the 4 pt rule beneath each headline act name, and beneath any two-line Sentinel Black line on the shirt. On the shirt the undyed cotton is the ground and no more than two of the shop's inks print, with no Kraft Paper. festival-mark.svg uses only the shop's inks or Kraft Paper, on a transparent ground.
palette_rules.opacity: Every ink prints solid, at 100%, or as a coarse halftone dot of that one ink, which is the only tint: roughly 20 to 25 lines per inch, picked against the size the piece actually prints at, as wharfside_shop_note.txt says, used only to carry the tonal washes of wharfside_artwork_master.png. No transparency, blend mode, gradient, drop shadow, fine screen or process rosette, and no overlay of any colour, black and white included, laid over the painting.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the palette hexes for type, rules, panels, icons, the mark or the painting's separations. No more inks than wharfside_shop_note.txt allows, white included, and no process colour build.
palette_rules.photography: wharfside_artwork_master.png is reproduced only by separating it into the shop's inks and the Kraft Paper ground, keeping its drawing and proportions (cropping allowed); it is not repainted, restyled, stretched or printed as a full-colour image. wharfside_wordmark_shed.jpg is the source the mark is recovered from, not artwork to place, and its weathered timber is not carried into the mark.
